prompt.context: You are the owner of a Laundromat in New York City.
prompt.question: What are some ways you can increase profits?

framework: Break profits into Revenues and Costs
Revenues: machine usage (coins, scan cards), ancillary supplies (detergent, softener, bleach), other goods and services
Costs: machines (upkeep and replacement), marketing, rent and utilities

brainstorming.prompt: What are ways to increase profits at a NYC Laundromat? Structure your answer around revenues and costs.

categories.name: Revenue — Machine Usage
ideas: Increase coin prices per wash/dry cycle
Introduce scan/loyalty cards to promote repeat business
Add more machines to increase capacity

categories.name: Revenue — Ancillary Products
ideas: Sell detergent, fabric softener, and bleach on-site
Offer vending machines with convenience items

categories.name: Revenue — Other Services
ideas: Offer wash-and-fold drop-off service at a premium
Partner with local businesses for pick-up/delivery laundry
Host events or live music to attract new customers and media attention

categories.name: Cost — Machines
ideas: Replace aging machines with energy-efficient models to cut utility costs
Lease rather than own machines to reduce capital outlay

categories.name: Cost — Rent & Utilities
ideas: Sublet unused floor space to another vendor
Convert part of the business to non-profit status by allowing a charity to use unused space, potentially reducing tax burden
Switch to off-peak energy usage where possible

categories.name: Cost — Marketing
ideas: Use low-cost guerrilla marketing (events, social media) instead of paid ads
Build loyalty through card-based promotions to reduce churn-related acquisition costs

recommendation: Focus first on revenue: introduce loyalty scan cards to drive repeat business and sell high-margin ancillary supplies (detergent, softener)
On the cost side, explore converting unused space to non-profit use or subletting it to reduce effective rent
risks: NYC rent increases could erode margin gains
Adding services (wash-and-fold) raises labor costs and complexity
next_steps: Audit current machine utilization and pricing vs. nearby competitors
Model incremental revenue from ancillary product sales
Explore legal and tax implications of non-profit space conversion
